title: Customs Amendment (Australia-United Arab Emirates Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement Implementation) Bill 2025
short_title: Customs Amendment (Australia-United Arab Emirates Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement Implementation) Bill 2025

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would amend the Customs Act 1901 to insert rules of origin for deciding whether goods imported from the United Arab Emirates (UAE) qualify for preferential tariff treatment under the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement.

New Division 1Q would treat goods as UAE originating if they are wholly obtained or produced in the UAE, made there from originating materials, or made from non-originating materials meeting product-specific rules, generally with a certificate of origin.

A companion Customs Tariff Amendment bill would set the rates, and Schedule 1 would commence on the later of Royal Assent and the Agreement's entry into force for Australia, and not at all if it never enters into force.
changes: Goods transported through a non-party would lose UAE originating status if they undergo further production there or are released to free circulation, beyond operations such as unloading, storing or repacking.
Importers could calculate qualifying value content using either the customs value or the ex-works price of the goods.
New Division 4N would let regulations impose record-keeping obligations on Australian producers and exporters claiming preferential tariffs in the UAE.
Authorised officers could require those exporters and producers to produce records or answer questions, and disclose them to a UAE customs official to verify a claim.
Customs duty collections are estimated to fall by $16 million in 2025-26, rising to $23 million a year by 2029-30.
summary.affected: Importers of goods from the UAE, Australian producers and exporters claiming UAE preferential tariffs, and authorised customs officers would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Julian Hill
speeches.brief: Introduced the Customs Tariff Amendment (Australia-United Arab Emirates Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement Implementation) Bill 2025 to establish preferential customs duty rates for UAE originating goods, maintain tariff concessions and continue excise-equivalent duties on specified fuel, alcohol, tobacco and petroleum products.

speeches.speaker: Tony Burke
speeches.brief: Declared that the Customs Amendment and Customs Tariff Amendment bills implementing the Australia-United Arab Emirates Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement would stand referred to the Federation Chamber for further consideration.

speeches.speaker: Anthony Chisholm
speeches.brief: Moved a timetable for consideration of the Universities Accord (Cutting Student Debt by 20 Per Cent) Bill 2025, the Early Childhood Education and Care (Strengthening Regulation of Early Education) Bill 2025 and Australia-United Arab Emirates trade bills from Tuesday, 29 July 2025 to Thursday, 31 July 2025, including limits on debate and scheduled votes.

speeches.speaker: Jenny McAllister
speeches.brief: Moved that the Customs Amendment and Customs Tariff Amendment bills be read a second time, outlining their implementation of the Australia-United Arab Emirates Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement, tariff preferences and expected benefits for trade, investment and exporters; the question was agreed to and the bills were read a second time.
